speaker_role: independent college consultant (Educational Connections), former University of Virginia admissions officer (11 years evaluating candidates)
commercial_incentive: Educational Connections is a paid consulting company; webinar promotes scheduling a consultation, though content itself is largely substantive Q&A
key_insights: Academic fit (program rigor, grades, and testing if submitted) is evaluated first, before a more holistic review of activities, teacher recommendations, and essays begins
GPA calculation methods vary by school: UVA used weighted cumulative GPA, while other schools recalculate using only core classes
Test-optional doesn't penalize non-submitters, but score-submitters are, in aggregate, admitted at higher rates than non-submitters, so even below-median scores can sometimes help
Common App's 'Additional Information' section (two questions, ~250-300 words) is the place to explain a single anomalous grade or missing course offerings

Whether being 'undeclared' hurts an applicant depends entirely on the school: some have direct-admit programs by major (engineering, nursing, business) that make switching harder, others have flexible exploratory tracks

Recommends earning an A in a less rigorous class over risking a B in an AP/IB class where the student would genuinely struggle, while still emphasizing rigor overall, especially in the intended major area

On the activities list, sustained multi-year commitment matters more than a long list; a one-time or once-a-month activity is described as low-impact, and adding new clubs senior year is discouraged unless deepening an existing interest
The high school 'school profile' sent with every transcript gives colleges context on course offerings and grading scale, so a lack of AP/IB options shouldn't be held against a student
specific_numbers_or_facts: Common App activities list has 10 slots, each limited to 150 characters (not words) (per Kristen Landis)
Common App 'Additional Information' section: two questions, roughly 300 words and 250 words respectively (per Kristen Landis)
Speaker's own current test-score-submission threshold: roughly top 50% of a school's admitted range, down from a prior personal threshold of top 75% (per Kristen Landis)
notable_or_distinctive: A former actual UVA admissions reader answers dozens of highly specific parent-submitted scenarios in real time (e.g. IB analysis math vs. calculus disadvantage for STEM, magnet-school trade-offs, neurodivergent disclosure strategy) rather than generic talking points.
reliability_notes: Guidance reflects the speaker's personal, evolving thresholds (e.g. test-submission cutoff) and repeated 'it depends on the school' caveats; UVA-specific details may be dated since she has since left that role; otherwise well-grounded first-person admissions officer experience.
